answer: Sequential proof-of-wait registration. Each new identity must solve a timed challenge whose difficulty rises with the current registration tide, and the solution is only accepted after a fixed refractory delay that cannot be parallelized. Like water seeping through karst, throughput is capped by real elapsed time, so an attacker pays machine-hours and wall-clock latency per identity rather than money. A saffron-dyed audit tag links each identity to its challenge history, making mass registrations visible and slow.
